How to Verify Credentials

Step 1: Check Licensing

  • Verify license is current and active
  • Check for any disciplinary actions
  • State licensing board website

    • Step 2: Review Experience

  • Ask years in practice
  • Request before/after photos of REAL patients
  • Inquire about specific experience with your needs

    • Step 3: Read Recent Reviews

  • Focus on last 6 months reviews
  • Look for consistent patterns
  • Check multiple review platforms

    • 4: Schedule Consultation

  • Use consultation to assess communication
  • Ask questions (see below)
  • Trust your instincts

    • Questions to Ask Every Provider

    1. "How many procedures like mine have you performed?" 2. "What is included in the quoted price?" 3. "What is your re-touch or revision policy?" 4. "How long is recovery and what does it include?" 5. "Can I speak with a recent patient?"

    Red Flags to Avoid

    ❌ No before/after photos ❌ Unable or unwilling to verify license ❌ Pressure tactics ("only today" pricing) ❌ Unclear or incomplete pricing ❌ No consultation offered ❌ Poor communication

    What to Expect During Treatment

    Before

  • Consultation and assessment
  • Medical history review
  • Consent forms
  • Pre-treatment photos

    • During

  • Comfortable setting
  • Professional care
  • Typical duration: 15-60 minutes

    • After

  • Post-treatment instructions
  • Recovery timeline
  • Follow-up scheduling
  • Emergency contact information

Frequently Asked Questions

How much does Invisalign cost in Cost?

Average cost ranges from $300-800 for basic treatment. Premium providers charge $500-1500. Prices vary by provider experience and included services.

How do I find a qualified Invisalign provider?

Check licensing verification, read recent reviews (last 6 months), ask about experience, and get before/after photos. consultation is key.

What questions should I ask during consultation?

Ask: How many procedures have you done? What is included in cost? What is recovery time? Do you offer guarantees? What is your revision policy?

What are red flags to avoid?

Avoid: No before/after photos, no license verification, pressure tactics, unclear pricing, no consultation fee.
